newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products - Arbitrages still play role.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products - Arbitrages still play role.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Tuesday, with gasoline steady, but fuel weaker.
Gas oil was looking a touch pressured as activity quietened on Tuesday after a sustained period of strength.
Traders said demand to fill the last Indian tender was declining and that while the arb eastwards was still workable, it was getting narrower.
"I don't think people are looking so much to take product east from the end of the month," said one.
Large Russian cargoes were looking for high fob quotes +$4, roughly the same for Italian spec 0.2 pct.
Gasoline was steady to firmer with traders quoting quotes high fob Med +$2.50/$3.0 for a 25kt premium unleaded cargo.

Traders said a number of players were looking into the possibility of shipping supply to the United States. "We're expecting to see the possibilities opening up over the next couple of weeks," one trader said.
A Dutch player was reported to have shifted two gasoline cargoes out of the region to the United States last week.
On the naphtha front, traders said the market remained fairly stagnant with not that much demand but not that much available material either.

High sulphur cracked cargo values fell, with many barrels reportedly available. Offers were heard around $76 fob, but buyers said closing deals was proving difficult, suggesting the price was being artificially driven down.
Floating price offers for mid-May were heard at fob high quotes plus $1.75.
Demand was so poor, an Italian trader was heard to have shipped Greek bunker spec material to Romania. The Portuguese electricity tender was lending the market little support.
The Russian straight-run market was quiet, with one Black Sea M-40 heard actively offered. -- London +44 171 542 8980
